question: Published costs (exposures, time, dose) and error rates of intraoperative fluoroscopic level localisation in thoracic and lumbar spine surgery
verification_method: DOI: api.crossref.org/works/<doi> title and first author match, plus the doi.org handle API returning 200. PMID: PubMed esummary title match and PubMed-listed DOI equal to the DOI. read_full_text=true means the full text or tables were read from PMC. Abstract-only entries were read from the PubMed efetch abstract.

categories.b_per_operation: per operation (whole procedure; localisation share not isolated unless stated)

claims.claim: Pre-incision needle localisation of the lumbar disc level under lateral C-arm fluoroscopy took a mean of 3.2 fluoroscopic acquisitions (range 1-12).
claims.quote: Table 1 cell: "Nr. of acquisitions | 3.2 (2.2; 1–12)". Methods: "the number of radiographic acquisitions in lateral view".
claims.authors: Prod'homme M, Grasset D, Lecocq M, Boscherini D
claims.title: Intraoperative disc level marking with needle: a technical note and prospective study on 30 patients
claims.caveat: Single centre, 30 patients, one needle per case, acquisitions counted for the landmarking step only. Levels above L5-S1 needed more: Discussion says "the need to move the imaging device and additional acquisitions for upper levels than L5-S1 from the sacrum reference on lateral fluoroscopic views".

claims.claim: The same localisation step used a mean of 4.3 s of fluoroscopy and 2.2 min of wall-clock time.
claims.quote: Table 1 cells: "Imaging duration (s) | 4.3 (2.8; 1–13)" and "Landmarking duration (min) | 2.2 (0.9; 1–5)". Abstract: "Mean time for landmarking was 2.22 [1–5] minutes."
claims.authors: Prod'homme M, Grasset D, Lecocq M, Boscherini D
claims.title: Intraoperative disc level marking with needle: a technical note and prospective study on 30 patients
claims.caveat: The format "x (y; a–b)" is printed without a legend. Read it as mean (SD; range); that reading is an inference.

claims.claim: The dose attributable to that localisation step was a DAP of 327 mGy·cm² and an effective dose of 0.032 mSv. L4-L5 and higher levels received more (0.040 mSv) than L5-S1 (0.025 mSv).
claims.quote: Results: "Average DAP was 327 mGy∙cm2. The mean E related to the imaging device was 0.032 mSv." Table 2 cells: "DAP (mGy∙cm2) | 327 (247; 61–1174)", "E (mSv) | 0.032 (0.020; 0.007–0.092)". Table 3: "L5-S1, E (mSv) | 0.025 (0.014; 0.007–0.066)", "L4-L5 and upper, E (mSv) | 0.040 (0.023; 0.008–0.092)".
claims.authors: Prod'homme M, Grasset D, Lecocq M, Boscherini D
claims.title: Intraoperative disc level marking with needle: a technical note and prospective study on 30 patients
claims.caveat: E was computed with PCXMC 2.0 from the DAP recorded after landmarking. It is a modelled effective dose, not a measured one.

claims.claim: Intraoperative localisation of upper thoracic levels with oblique C-arm radiographs and a methylene-blue mark took a median of 3 radiographs and a median of 2 min 25 s.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The median radiographing times of all the patients was 3, and the median radiographing duration was 2 min and 25 s." Table 3 cells: "RT (times) 3 (2.5–4)", "RD (h:m:s) 0:02:25 (0:01:36–0:03:28)".
claims.location: Abstract; Results; Table 3 (per-patient values in Table 2)
claims.authors: Huang H, Wei M, Fan J, Peng R, Ding X, Xi J
claims.title: Oblique radiograph with methylene blue marking: A reliable technique for upper thoracic level localization
claims.setting: Upper thoracic (C7-T6) intradural tumours, Xiangya, retrospective, n=33
claims.caveat: The technique is new: the oblique angle and table height are planned from preoperative MRI or CT to cut shots, so this is not standard counting. There is no comparator arm. The per-patient maximum in Table 2 is 0:10:50. The abstract gives BMI 24.3 ± 0.7 where Table 3 gives 24.3 ± 3.9.

claims.claim: In thoracic spine surgery, localisation took 15 min with the standard fluoroscopy technique and 3 min with a CT-placed fiducial.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The localization time with the fiducial was reduced dramatically (3 min vs 15 min of the standard technique)."
claims.authors: Mongardi L, Visani J, Mantovani G, Olivetti ME, Scerrati A, Cultrera F, Ricciardi L, De Bonis P, Cavallo MA, Lofrese G
claims.title: Ct guided reference markers for spinal dorsal lesions: A safe and valuable tool impacting intraoperative localization time
claims.setting: Thoracic ("dorsal") lesions, Ferrara, prospective, 19 fiducial vs 11 fluoroscopy
claims.caveat: Abstract only; the full text is paywalled and not in Unpaywall. The abstract calls this "localization time", not fluoroscopy time. Two secondary sources misreport the study: Strong et al. 2022 (J Neurosurg Spine 36:792) swaps the group sizes to "11 ... fiducial ... 19 ... standard fluoroscopy" and says fiducials "reduced radiation exposure", and Jesse 2025 calls the difference "duration of fluoroscopy exposure". Upadhyaya 2012 reports the identical 3 vs 15 min, but only in its press release (see that entry). The two studies cannot be told apart on this number without the full texts.

claims.claim: The DAP attributable to localisation was 16 in the fluoroscopy group and 20 in the fiducial group, both printed as "Gy-cm2".
claims.quote: Abstract: "The average DAP (effective dose) for the fiducial group was 20 Gy-cm2 compared with 16 Gy-cm2 of the traditional group."
claims.authors: Mongardi L, Visani J, Mantovani G, Olivetti ME, Scerrati A, Cultrera F, Ricciardi L, De Bonis P, Cavallo MA, Lofrese G
claims.title: Ct guided reference markers for spinal dorsal lesions: A safe and valuable tool impacting intraoperative localization time
claims.caveat: The unit is implausible as printed. 16 Gy·cm² is 1,600 cGy·cm², about 17 times the whole-procedure DAP Grelat 2016 reports for a lumbar microdiscectomy, and the abstract conflates DAP with effective dose. Do not quote this without the full text. The fiducial arm is higher, not lower.

claims.claim: The abstract says only that intraoperative localisation fluoroscopy time was "greatly reduced" with a fiducial screw, compared with 26 historical controls localised by fluoroscopy alone. It gives no number.
claims.quote: Abstract: "the authors found that the intraoperative localization fluoroscopy time was greatly reduced when a fiducial screw localization technique was employed." Conclusions: "There is a reduction in the amount of intraoperative fluoroscopy time needed for localization in the fiducial screw group."
claims.authors: Upadhyaya CD, Wu JC, Chin CT, Balamurali G, Mummaneni PV
claims.title: Avoidance of wrong-level thoracic spine surgery: intraoperative localization with preoperative percutaneous fiducial screw placement
claims.caveat: The full text is paywalled; thejns.org serves the abstract only.

claims.claim: Fluoroscopic localisation time was 15 min with needle counting and 3 min with a fiducial screw. This figure comes only from the JNS press release, not from the paper.
claims.quote: Newswise / JNS press release, 4 Nov 2011: "the surgeon found that the fluoroscopic localization time is much shorter when one fiducial screw is used: 3 minutes rather than 15 minutes." The same release describes the control arm as "localization of specific vertebrae was made using fluoroscopy and a series of percutaneous needles to aid in counting vertebral levels".
claims.location: https://www.newswise.com/articles/thoracic-spine-surgery-a-new-technique-to-avoid-operating-on-the-wrong-level (a secondary source issued by the journal)
claims.authors: Upadhyaya CD, Wu JC, Chin CT, Balamurali G, Mummaneni PV
claims.title: Avoidance of wrong-level thoracic spine surgery: intraoperative localization with preoperative percutaneous fiducial screw placement
claims.caveat: NOT VERIFIED IN THE PRIMARY TEXT. Strong 2022 repeats it as fluoroscopy time "(3 vs 15 minutes)", and Jesse 2025 as "reduced by 12 min". Cite the paper for the qualitative reduction only, unless the full text is read.

claims.claim: Conventional pre-incision localisation for lumbar MIS surgery (palpation plus a Kirschner wire) took 7.37 min and 2.29 C-arm shots. A novel locator took 3.85 min and 1.29 shots.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The mean localization time of patients in groups A and B were 7.37±3.77 and 3.85±2.45 minutes, respectively. The mean number of preoperative C-arm fluoroscopy use in groups A and B were 2.29 and 1.29."
claims.authors: Gu G, Zhang H, He S, Jia J, Fu Q, Zhou X
claims.title: Preoperative localization methods for minimally invasive surgery in lumbar spine: comparisons between a novel method and conventional methods
claims.caveat: Abstract only. Prospective but non-randomised: the first 100 patients were conventional and the next 120 used the locator. No wrong-level surgery occurred in either group. This localisation is incision planning for MIS and includes the level.

claims.claim: Conventional pre-operative localisation for MIS-TLIF in overweight patients took 7.03 min; a localisation system cut it to 4.73 min.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The mean pre-operative localisation time was 4.73 minutes (sd 0.84) in Group A and 7.03 minutes (sd 1.51) in Group B (p < 0.001)."
claims.authors: Fan G, Fu Q, Zhang J, Zhang H, Gu X, Wang C, Gu G, Guan X, Fan Y, He S
claims.title: Radiation reduction of minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion with localisation system in overweight patients: practical technique
claims.caveat: Abstract only. Group B is conventional. Overweight patients; prospective multicentre. Same group as Gu 2013.

claims.claim: Conventional localisation took 5.95 min before PTED and 6.63 min before MIS-TLIF; the localisation system cut these to 4.64 and 4.00 min.
claims.quote: Table 2 cell: "Location time, min | 4.64±1.04 | 5.95±1.21 | <.001". Table 3 cell: "Location time, min | 4.00±0.36 | 6.63±1.16 | <.001".
claims.location: Results, Tables 2 (PTED) and 3 (MISTLIF). The tables are images and were read as images.
claims.authors: Fan G, Zhang H, Gu X, Wang C, Guan X, Fan Y, He S
claims.title: Significant reduction of fluoroscopy repetition with lumbar localization system in minimally invasive spine surgery: A prospective study
claims.caveat: Group B is conventional. The per-operation fluoroscopy counts in the same tables cover the whole procedure (see the b entry).

claims.claim: Conventional (pedicle-projection) localisation for single-level lumbar UBE used 4.4 fluoroscopy shots and 1.8 localisation adjustments, and took 8.5 min to confirm. Robot-assisted localisation used 2.1 shots but took 12.5 min, of which 8.2 min was registration.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The r-UBE group was associated with a lower fluoroscopy frequency (2.1 ± 1.3 vs. 4.4 ± 1.8; mean difference - 2.3, 95% CI - 3.0 to - 1.6; p < 0.01) and fewer localization adjustments (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 1.8 ± 0.9 ...). However, localization confirmation time was significantly longer in the r-UBE group (12.5 ± 3.5 min vs. 8.5 ± 2.5 min ...), primarily due to the registration process (8.2 ± 2.8 min)."
claims.authors: Huang K, Zhang T, Li G, Tang X, Li H, Wang Y, Zhang J
claims.title: Robot-assisted versus pedicle projection localization in unilateral biportal endoscopic spine surgery: a trade-off analysis of fluoroscopy use, procedural time, and learning curve
claims.setting: Lumbar single-level UBE, Xuzhou, n=32 robot vs 54 conventional
claims.caveat: Abstract only; paywalled. Retrospective, non-randomised. This localisation finds the endoscopic entry point, which includes the level. The abstract lists fluoroscopy frequency among the localisation outcomes but does not say it is restricted to the localisation phase.

claims.claim: Fluoroscopic skin marking before minimally invasive lumbar surgery took 122.5 s, 8.2 x-rays and 3.8 mGy with a conventional C-arm. Instrument tracking cut it to 16.3 s, 1.8 x-rays and 0.7 mGy.
claims.authors: Wang TY, Hamouda F, Mehta VA, Sankey EW, Yarbrough C, Lark R, Abd-El-Barr MM
claims.title: Effect of Instrument Navigation on C-arm Radiation and Time during Spinal Procedures: A Clinical Evaluation
claims.caveat: Skin marking is incision planning and is not confined to level identification. The comparison was internally randomised by coin flip, over 16 skin-marking tasks across 3 surgeons. A TrackX employee is a co-author.

claims.claim: A technical note estimates that MIS entry-site planning with loose radiopaque markers "typically" took 6-12 fluoroscopic images, against 1-2 with a grid.
claims.quote: Results: "With the use of the radiopaque localizer grid, one or two images are sufficient to determine the ideal entry site instead of six to twelve images typically obtained prior to its use."
claims.authors: Kim KD, Li W, Galloway CL
claims.title: Use of a radiopaque localizer grid to reduce radiation exposure
claims.journal: Annals of Surgical Innovation and Research
claims.caveat: This is an author estimate, not a measurement: no cohort and no statistics. It concerns MIS entry-site planning, which includes the level.

claims.claim: A whole lumbar microdiscectomy used a mean of 10.2 s of fluoroscopy and a DAP of 94.2 cGy·cm² per procedure; here fluoroscopy serves mainly to confirm the level.
claims.quote: Abstract: "Often, a few snapshots during the procedure are necessary to validate the level or to position the implant." and "For these procedures, the dose area product (DAP) was 94.2 ± 198.4 cGy·cm(2), and the fluoroscopic time was 10.2 ± 16.9 seconds."
claims.authors: Grelat M, Greffier J, Sabatier P, Dauzac C, Lonjon G, Debono B, Le Roy J, Kouyoumdjïan P, Lonjon N
claims.title: Assessment of the Radiation Exposure of Surgeons and Patients During a Lumbar Microdiskectomy and a Cervical Microdiskectomy: A French Prospective Multicenter Study
claims.caveat: Abstract only. Four French centres, prospective. The abstract gives 134 patients in total and does not split them between lumbar and cervical. Imaging is not attributed to localisation versus other uses. The SD exceeds the mean, so the distribution is heavily right-skewed.

claims.claim: Microendoscopic spine surgery with dedicated localisation devices used an average of 3.1 s of fluoroscopy and 0.26 mGy per operation.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The average radiation exposure was 0.26 mGy (range 0.10-1.15 mGy), and the average total fluoroscopy time was 3.1 s (range 1-7 s)."
claims.authors: Takami M, Elwany A, Destandau J
claims.title: Accuracy and evaluation of irradiation of novel localization devices with unique three-dimensional structures in microendoscopic spine surgery
claims.journal: European Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery & Traumatology
claims.caveat: Abstract only. Measured in the last 100 consecutive patients with a dosimeter on the fluoroscope. This is the whole operation, using the authors' localisation devices, which is not the conventional baseline.

claims.claim: Conventional overweight MIS-TLIF used 40.67 s of fluoroscopy per operation, against 26.42 s with the localisation system.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The mean fluoroscopy exposure time was 26.42 seconds (sd 5.91) in Group A and 40.67 seconds (sd 8.18) in Group B (p < 0.001)."
claims.authors: Fan G, Fu Q, Zhang J, Zhang H, Gu X, Wang C, Gu G, Guan X, Fan Y, He S
claims.title: Radiation reduction of minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion with localisation system in overweight patients: practical technique
claims.caveat: This is the whole operation, including percutaneous screw guidance, not localisation alone. The abstract's effective dose (0.0383 vs 0.0217 mSv) is to the surgeon.

claims.claim: Conventional PTED used 33.85 fluoroscopy shots and 30.53 s per operation, and conventional MIS-TLIF 36.21 shots and 32.82 s. The estimated patient effective dose was about 0.57-0.58 mSv.
claims.quote: Table 2 cells: "Fluoroscopy times | 24.98±7.87 | 33.85±8.04", "Exposure time, s | 22.18±7.30 | 30.53±7.56", "Estimated effective dose, mSv | 0.41±0.13 | 0.57±0.14". Table 3 cells: "Fluoroscopy times | 28.82±5.76 | 36.21±5.49", "Exposure time, s | 25.41±5.52 | 32.82±5.03", "Estimated effective dose, mSv | 0.45±0.09 | 0.58±0.09".
claims.authors: Fan G, Zhang H, Gu X, Wang C, Guan X, Fan Y, He S
claims.title: Significant reduction of fluoroscopy repetition with lumbar localization system in minimally invasive spine surgery: A prospective study
claims.caveat: This is the whole procedure, dominated by puncture and screw guidance, so it is not attributable to level localisation. DAP and E were estimated from exposure time by regression, not measured.

claims.claim: Thoracic surgery localised by fluoroscopic counting from the craniocervical or lumbosacral junction, before incision and after exposure, used 18 s of intraoperative fluoroscopy and 0.11 mSv. The data are sparse.
claims.quote: Table 2 cells: "Duration of intraoperative fluoroscopy, [s] | 18 (±14), 3 (6.5 %) | 10 (±13), 19 (26.8 %) | 0.33"; "Effective dose of intraoperative fluoroscopy, [mSv] | 0.11 (±0.14), 2 (4.3 %) | 0.05 (±0.07), 18 (25.4 %) | 0.32". Methods: "counting the vertebrae from the craniocervical or lumbosacral junctions in the direction of the index vertebra under fluoroscopic control ... before skin incision and after exposure".
claims.authors: Jesse CM, Kannathasan A, Schär RT, Goldberg J, Raabe A, Gralla J, Kaesmacher J, Dobrocky T, Piechowiak EI
claims.title: The utility of preoperative computed tomography-guided screw marking in thoracic spine surgery
claims.setting: Thoracic, Bern, retrospective case-control, 46 control vs 71 screw
claims.caveat: Only 3 and 2 of the 46 control patients had data, so these numbers cannot carry weight. Total OR occupancy did not differ: 199 min (control) vs 216 min (screw), p=0.26, Table 3.

claims.claim: Operations on patients whose wrong level was initially exposed were longer at the median: 85 vs 80 min for lumbar decompression and 80 vs 67.5 min for discectomy. The SBNS recommends three intraoperative x-rays per lumbar case.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The SBNS recommends three x-rays for intra-operative spinal localisation - one prior to incision, the second after exposure of the laminae and before the commencement of decompression, and the third at the end of the operation" ... "The median duration of surgery was 80 minutes for lumbar decompression and 67.5 minutes for lumbar discectomy. The median duration of surgery in patients in whom the wrong level was initially exposed was 85 minutes for lumbar decompression and 80 minutes for lumbar discectomy."
claims.authors: Dablouk MO, Sajjad J, Lim C, Kaar G, O'Sullivan MGJ
claims.title: Intra-operative imaging for spinal level localisation in lumbar surgery
claims.caveat: Abstract only. The wrong-level group has 13 cases and no statistical test is given in the abstract.

claims.claim: Formal radiologist reads of intraoperative localisation and post-instrumentation radiographs arrived a median of 128 min after imaging and cost each patient $32-34.
claims.quote: Abstract: "Four hundred eighty-one intraoperative localization and post-instrumentation radiographs from 360 patients revealed a median delay of 128 minutes between imaging and completion of the interpretive report. Only 38.9% of reports were completed before the conclusion of surgery." ... "Each patient was charged $32 to $34 for the interpretation fee".
claims.authors: Lin RT, Dalton JF, Como CJ, Chang AY, Tang MY, Oyekan AA, Sadhwani S, Wawrose RA, Lee JY, Shaw JD
claims.title: Formal Radiologist Interpretations of Intraoperative Spine Radiographs Have Low Clinical Value
claims.setting: All elective spine surgery, Pittsburgh, 360 patients
claims.caveat: Abstract only. This is the cost of the radiology read, not of acquisition. Plain radiographs, not fluoroscopy.

claims.claim: During open lumbar microdiscectomy, where x-rays are used for localisation, the surgeon received 0.16-0.21 mR per case.
claims.number: thyroid/eye 0.16 ± 0.22, chest 0.21 ± 0.23, hand 0.20 ± 0.14 mR per open case
claims.quote: Abstract: "The average radiation exposure to the surgeon during open cases was thyroid/eye 0.16 ± 0.22 mR, chest 0.21 ± 0.23 mR, and hand 0.20 ± 0.14 mR." ... "Standing in a substerile room during x-ray localization in open cases is not fully protective."
claims.authors: Mariscalco MW, Yamashita T, Steinmetz MP, Krishnaney AA, Lieberman IH, Mroz TE
claims.title: Radiation exposure to the surgeon during open lumbar microdiscectomy and minimally invasive microdiscectomy: a prospective, controlled trial
claims.setting: Open vs MIS lumbar microdiscectomy, Cleveland Clinic, 10+10
claims.caveat: Abstract only. This is surgeon dose, not patient dose. The abstract gives no fluoroscopy time or image count, although the methods say total fluoroscopy time was collected.

claims.claim: In 100 consecutive single-surgeon lumbar discectomies, the level the surgeon had exposed, checked by intraoperative x-ray, was the intended one in 85%, so 15% were initially exposed at the wrong level.
claims.quote: Abstract: "After exposure, the surgeon was asked to identify the level exposed, which was confirmed by intraoperative x-ray." ... "Four patients had transitional vertebrae. The intended level was initially exposed in 85% of cases. Age and level of pathology (P < .05) were identified as factors predictive of a mismatch between intraoperative level of exposure and preoperative level of pathology."
claims.authors: Ammerman JM, Ammerman MD, Dambrosia J, Ammerman BJ
claims.title: A prospective evaluation of the role for intraoperative x-ray in lumbar discectomy. Predictors of incorrect level exposure
claims.caveat: Abstract only; the Elsevier full text is not open access. The abstract never prints "15%"; that figure is 100 − 85. The abstract does not say whether a localising film was taken before incision, or whether the "x-ray" was fluoroscopy or a plain film. The earlier bibliography DOI 10.1016/j.surneu.2006.05.056 is a different paper: Samadani et al., "Stereotactic biopsy of brain stem masses", Surg Neurol 66:484-490. The correct DOI is 10.1016/j.surneu.2006.05.069, which refs.bib now carries.

claims.claim: In 301 lumbar decompressions or discectomies across three surgeons, the incorrect level was initially exposed in 13 (4.3%). No wrong-level operation was completed.
claims.quote: Abstract: "There were no cases of wrong-level surgery. The incorrect spinal level was initially exposed in 13 cases (4.3%). 10 of these had x-ray 2 only, 1 had x-ray 1, 1 had x-rays 1 and 2, and 1 had all 3 x-rays."
claims.authors: Dablouk MO, Sajjad J, Lim C, Kaar G, O'Sullivan MGJ
claims.title: Intra-operative imaging for spinal level localisation in lumbar surgery
claims.caveat: Abstract only; retrospective logbook review. The definition matches Ammerman.

claims.claim: Under the IRACE protocol (wire in the spinous process, lateral fluoroscopy before incision, a nurse confirming the level, and fluoroscopy again before laminotomy), a wrong level was initially explored in 1 of 818 microdiscectomies (0.12%).
claims.quote: Abstract: "In 1 (0.12%) of 818 surgical procedures a wrong level was initially explored."
claims.authors: Irace C, Corona C
claims.title: How to avoid wrong-level and wrong-side errors in lumbar microdiscectomy
claims.caveat: Abstract only. Retrospective, and all cases used the protocol, so the rate is the protocol's residual error, not a baseline.

claims.claim: Before imaging, palpation-based level marking between T4 and L2 was accurate in only 40% of 30 prospective patients: 26.7% were one level off and 33.3% two levels off.
claims.number: 40% accurate; 26.7% off by one; 33.3% off by two
claims.quote: Abstract: "Accuracy of pathology related spine level localization using anatomical landmarks was only 40%." Results: "Sixty percent of the patients had inaccurate spine level localization utilizing conventional clinical palpatory methods, while 26.7% were one spinal level inaccurate, and 33.3% were two spinal level(s), respectively."
claims.authors: Tee JW, Rutges J, Marion T, Street J, Paquette S, Ailon T, Kwon BK, Dvorak M, Boyd M
claims.title: Factors predictive of topographical accuracy in spine level localization
claims.setting: Posterior T4-L2 surgery, Vancouver, prospective, n=30
claims.caveat: This measures the error before any image, verified by a PA radiograph with a Target Tape grid. It shows why localisation images are needed, and is not a fluoroscopic counting error.

claims.claim: One thoracic operation in the fluoroscopic-counting control group was at the wrong level (1/46, 2.2%), against none of 71 with a preoperative CT-guided screw.
claims.quote: Discussion: "In comparison, one WLS occurred in our control group, accounting for 2.2 % of the patients who underwent surgery." Abstract: "WLS occurred in only one patient in the control group and none in the screw group."
claims.authors: Jesse CM, Kannathasan A, Schär RT, Goldberg J, Raabe A, Gralla J, Kaesmacher J, Dobrocky T, Piechowiak EI
claims.title: The utility of preoperative computed tomography-guided screw marking in thoracic spine surgery
claims.caveat: Retrospective case-control and underpowered.

claims.claim: Using dedicated localisation devices, 8 of 8,240 microendoscopic operations (0.097%) were at the wrong level.
claims.quote: Abstract: "Eight (0.097 %) patients had undergone wrong-level surgery."
claims.authors: Takami M, Elwany A, Destandau J
claims.title: Accuracy and evaluation of irradiation of novel localization devices with unique three-dimensional structures in microendoscopic spine surgery
claims.journal: European Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery & Traumatology
claims.caveat: Abstract only; retrospective, 1993-2012.

claims.claim: In a NASS survey, 68% of responding surgeons reported wrong-level localisation at some point in their careers. Fluoroscopy was the imaging used for localisation by 89% (thoracic) and 86% (lumbar).
claims.quote: Abstract: "Fluoroscopy was the most commonly used imaging technique for thoracic and lumbar surgeries (89% and 86%, respectively)" ... "Sixty-eight percent of surgeons admitted to wrong-level localization, some of which were rectified intraoperatively, during their careers." Background: "Wrong-level exposure is documented in 0.32% to 15% of cases."
claims.authors: Mayer JE, Dang RP, Duarte Prieto GF, Cho SK, Qureshi SA, Hecht AC
claims.title: Analysis of the techniques for thoracic- and lumbar-level localization during posterior spine surgery and the occurrence of wrong-level surgery: results from a national survey
claims.caveat: Self-reported, 173 of 2,338 surgeons (7.4% response). The 0.32-15% range is background citing others; its upper bound corresponds to Ammerman.

claims.claim: Placing a gold fiducial before surgery, under fluoroscopy or CT guidance, carried a mean radiation dose of 183.43 mGy, a mean fluoroscopy time of 3.92 min and a procedure time of about 51-52 min.
claims.quote: Results: "The mean radiation dose was 183.43 mGy (range, 13–805 mGy), and the mean FL time was 3.92 minutes (range, 0.4–15.2 minutes). The average radiation dose for CT-guided placement (258.92 mGy) was higher than the average radiation dose for FL-guided placement (164.43 mGy), though the average procedural time was similar (51.19 minutes for CT and 52.09 minutes for FL)."
claims.authors: Siminski CP, Carr CM, Kallmes DF, Oien MP, Atkinson JLD, Benson JC, Diehn FE, Kim DK, Liebo GB, Lehman VT, Madhavan AA, Mark IT, Morris PP, Shlapak DP, Verdoorn JT, Morris JM
claims.title: Fluoroscopy- and CT-Guided Gold Fiducial Marker Placement for Intraoperative Localization during Spinal Surgery: Review of 179 Cases at a Single Institution-Technique and Safety Profile
claims.caveat: This is the cost of the separate preoperative procedure, not of intraoperative localisation. All 179 operations were at the correct level.

claims.claim: CT-guided screw marking before thoracic surgery took 25 min and delivered 6.8 mSv. Afterwards a single fluoroscopy image before incision sufficed.
claims.quote: Table 2 cells: "Duration of CT-guided screw marking, [min], mean (±SD) | – | 25 (±10)"; "Effective dose for CT-guided screw marking, [mSv], mean (±SD) | – | 6.8 (±3.7)". Methods: "Before skin incision, a single fluoroscopy image was obtained to verify the index level with the previously inserted screw."
claims.authors: Jesse CM, Kannathasan A, Schär RT, Goldberg J, Raabe A, Gralla J, Kaesmacher J, Dobrocky T, Piechowiak EI
claims.title: The utility of preoperative computed tomography-guided screw marking in thoracic spine surgery
claims.caveat: The marking dose (6.8 mSv) is more than 60 times the control group's intraoperative fluoroscopy dose (0.11 mSv, n=2).

claims.claim: With CT-placed gold fiducials, intraoperative fluoroscopy for thoracic localisation was 0.06-0.35 s per case, and the CT placement took a mean of 14.3 min.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The average CT intervention time from the planning scout to the final control time was 14.3 min." Table 2 column "IntraoperativeFluoroscopy Time (in Seconds)": 0.1, 0.06, 0.09, 0.2, 0.09, 0.07, 0.06, 0.2, 0.19, 0.35.
claims.authors: Keil F, Hagemes F, Setzer M, Behmanesh B, Marquardt G, Hattingen E, Prinz V, Czabanka M, Bruder M
claims.title: Minimal Invasive Pre-Op CT-Guided Gold-Fiducials in Local Anesthesia for Easy Level Localization in Thoracic Spine Surgery
claims.caveat: There is no control arm. Of the 8 patients with full-spine imaging, 2 had a lumbarised S1.

claims.claim: A CT-placed marking wire cut radiation exposure to OR personnel by more than 90% in non-instrumented thoracic cases.
claims.quote: Abstract: "Radiation exposure to operating room personnel could be reduced by more than 90% in all non-instrumented cases."
claims.authors: Ahmadi SA, Slotty PJ, Schröter C, Kröpil P, Steiger HJ, Eicker SO
claims.title: Marking wire placement for improved accuracy in thoracic spinal surgery
claims.caveat: Abstract only. The absolute values are not in the abstract.

claims.claim: After CT-guided coil marking, "typically a single lateral radiograph" is needed intraoperatively. This is an assertion, not a measurement.
claims.quote: Abstract: "Intraoperatively, typically a single lateral radiograph is required to visualize the coil and the level."
claims.authors: Castle-Kirszbaum M, Maingard J, Goldschlager T, Chandra RV
claims.title: Preoperative coil localization for spinal surgery: technical note
claims.caveat: This is a technical note with no measured cohort. Kam 2024 (ANZ J Surg 94:840, PMID 38553888) collected fluoroscopy usage for the same technique, but its abstract reports no number.

claims.claim: On 20 test-rig and 3 phantom set-ups in orthopaedic trauma, re-finding a C-arm position by conventional scout imaging took an average of 7 scout images (range 3-12) and 49 s. Navigated repositioning needed no scout images and took 46 s.
claims.number: 7 scout images (3-12); 49 s conventional vs 46 s navigated
claims.quote: Abstract: "Retrieving a given C-arm position with the conventional non-navigated technique required an average of 7 scout images (range, 3 to 12 images). In contrast, navigation-assisted repositioning did not necessitate a single scout image." ... "Average positioning times were comparable when navigating the C-arm (46 seconds, 95% CI 41 to 51 seconds) and in scout image-based positioning (49 seconds, 95% CI 44 to 53 seconds)."
claims.authors: Matthews F, Hoigne DJ, Weiser M, Wanner GA, Regazzoni P, Suhm N, Messmer P
claims.title: Navigating the fluoroscope's C-arm back into position: an accurate and practicable solution to cut radiation and optimize intraoperative workflow
claims.setting: Orthopaedic trauma, test rig and phantom
claims.caveat: NOT SPINE AND NOT CLINICAL: test rig and phantoms. The lead "C-arm positioning 46/49 s" is confirmed, but 46 s is the navigated arm and 49 s the conventional arm. Cite it only for scout images per repositioning, not as a spine localisation cost.

claims.claim: In ACDF, one localisation radiograph took 823 s from acquisition to interpretation on conventional film and 100 s digitally.
claims.quote: Abstract: "The mean time for conventional radiography was 823 seconds (standard deviation [SD], 159), and for digital, it was 100 seconds (SD, 34; p<.001)."
claims.authors: Steinmetz MP, Mroz TE, Krishnaney A, Modic M
claims.title: Conventional versus digital radiographs for intraoperative cervical spine-level localization: a prospective time and cost analysis
claims.caveat: CERVICAL, and a plain radiograph with a spinal needle in the disc, not fluoroscopy. Abstract only. n=10 vs 8.

leads_status.ammerman2006: VERIFIED: Surg Neurol 2006;66(5):470-3, PMID 17084188, DOI 10.1016/j.surneu.2006.05.069. The abstract says "85% initially exposed at intended level"; 15% is derived. The old bib DOI 10.1016/j.surneu.2006.05.056 is Samadani et al. (brain-stem biopsy).
leads_status.mongardi2021: VERIFIED from the abstract: 3 vs 15 min localisation time; DAP 20 vs 16 "Gy-cm2", with a doubtful unit and the fiducial arm higher. Two reviews misquote it (Strong 2022 swaps the arms; Jesse 2025 calls it fluoroscopy duration).
leads_status.upadhyaya2012: IDENTIFIERS VERIFIED, NUMBER NOT. The abstract is qualitative only ("greatly reduced"). "3 vs 15 min" appears only in the JNS/Newswise press release, not in any text read from the paper.
leads_status.hsu2008: VERIFIED identifiers (J Spinal Disord Tech 21:72-5, PMID 18418141). NO time, shot or dose number in the abstract: 4 morbidly obese patients, PMMA "easily identified". The full text is paywalled. Nothing numeric is citable.
leads_status.paolini2005: VERIFIED identifiers (Br J Neurosurg 19:74-6, PMID 16147592). NO numbers beyond 6 patients and no errors ("identified easily and immediately"). Useful only for the sentence "Intraoperative fluoroscopy is traditionally used to count the vertebrae throughout the whole spine. In the high thoracic spine, counting the vertebrae is often hampered by the scapular shadows."
leads_status.irace_corona: VERIFIED: Irace & Corona 2010, J Neurosurg Spine 12:660-5, PMID 20515352: 1/818 (0.12%) wrong level initially explored. No other Irace/Corona radiographic study was found. Irace & Usai 2012 (Patient Saf Surg 6:14) is a commentary without data.
leads_status.matthews2007: VERIFIED but NOT SPINE: trauma test rig and phantom; 7 scout images per conventional repositioning; 49 s conventional vs 46 s navigated.
leads_status.time_motion: No dedicated time-motion study of level localisation was found. The closest are Wang 2020 (task timing of skin marking with a conventional C-arm: 122.5 s, 8.2 x-rays), Huang K 2026 (localisation confirmation time 8.5 min), and Bullert 2026 (Orthopadie, PMID 42053630, DOI 10.1007/s00132-026-04834-9; a motorised C-arm compared with a standard C-arm; the abstract gives only percentage changes for the whole procedure, not localisation).
leads_status.searched_no_number: Checked and found to carry no localisation cost figure: Binning & Schmidt 2010 (Spine 35:1821), Madaelil 2017 (Spine 42:E624, which says "Further studies are needed to quantify changes in operative time and radiation exposure"), Ishak 2020 (Spine 45:1720, the same statement), Kam 2024 (ANZ J Surg 94:840, which collected fluoroscopy usage but reports no number in the abstract), Güvercin 2025 (Ulus Travma Acil Cerrahi Derg 31:371, qualitative "decrease in number of fluoroscopic images" and no number in the full text), Thambiraj 2012, Chin 2017, Singh 2009, Kinon 2020, Nowitzke 2008, Anaizi 2015, Cruickshank 2025, and the Loggia 2026 cadaver ultrasound study (98% accuracy, 49/50 levels, cadaver).
